thought.text: `python3` isn't available in the sandbox — that's why the token was empty. Let me extract the token with sed instead.

reasoning_content:
Ah — `python3: command not found` inside the subshell. Interesting — but earlier I was able to use python3 successfully? Wait, in the first login attempt I ran `python3 -c ... 2>/dev/null`, and the error was suppressed. So in this sandbox python3 doesn't exist! Let me check which interpreters are available. In fact, the first attempt was also producing an empty token. So I need another way to parse JSON: grep/sed, or jq if it's available.

Wait — but that earlier command `curl ... | python3 -c '...' 2>/dev/null` — python3 wasn't found and was outputting an error to /dev/null. So python3 isn't available on the host. Let me check for jq, or use sed to extract the token.

action.command:
cd /workspace/deployment
which jq sed python python3.12 2>/dev/null
RESP=$(curl -sk --resolve api.localhost:443:127.0.0.1 -X POST https://api.localhost/api/v1/auth/login/ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"admin","password":"Admin!LocalDev123"}')
TOKEN=$(printf '%s' "$RESP" | sed -n 's/.*"access":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
echo "token_len=${#TOKEN}"
echo "$TOKEN" > /tmp/token.txt
echo '=== auth/user ==='
curl -sk --resolve api.localhost:443:127.0.0.1 https://api.localhost/api/v1/auth/user/ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"; echo
echo '=== projects ==='
curl -sk --resolve api.localhost:443:127.0.0.1 https://api.localhost/api/v1/projects/ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' | head -c 500
echo '=== WebDAV PROPFIND with token ==='
curl -sk --resolve files.localhost:443:127.0.0.1 -X PROPFIND -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' https://files.localhost/ | head -c 500
echo '=== QGIS WMS GetCapabilities ==='
curl -sk --resolve qgis.localhost:443:127.0.0.1 "https://qgis.localhost/ows/?SERVICE=WMS&REQUEST=GetCapabilities" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -o /tmp/wms_caps.xml -w 'HTTP %{http_code} size=%{size_download}\n'
head -c 250 /tmp/wms_caps.xml; echo
echo '=== QGIS WFS GetCapabilities ==='
curl -sk --resolve qgis.localhost:443:127.0.0.1 "https://qgis.localhost/ows/?SERVICE=WFS&REQUEST=GetCapabilities" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -o /tmp/wfs_caps.xml -w 'HTTP %{http_code} size=%{size_download}\n'
head -c 250 /tmp/wfs_caps.xml; echo
